name: Low-Bandwidth Knowledge and Operations OS
promise: Preserve context and expose the next safe action when bandwidth is low.
completion_criteria: One SourceRecord path preserves capture, checksum, provenance, retrieval citation, and projection ownership.
Generated Observer notes cannot be ingested back as new canonical sources.
JARVIS presents and approves actions without duplicating storage or domain logic.
Unique Ryos and master-plan behavior is ported or rejected before their runtimes are retired.
Daily operation retains deterministic fallbacks when providers or credentials are unavailable.

waves.objective: Prove capture to PKOS to Observer projection with one SourceRecord fixture.
waves.acceptance: The source is content-addressed and cited; the generated note is stable and excluded from re-ingestion.

waves.objective: Inventory Ryos and master-plan behaviors against dotfiles and Observer.
waves.acceptance: Every unique behavior has a test-backed port, explicit rejection, or preserved historical owner.

waves.objective: Connect a JARVIS action preview to canonical services without copied state.
waves.acceptance: Preview, approval, execution receipt, failure, and recovery use owned APIs or file contracts.

waves.objective: Widen PKOS capture path to real day-to-day intake stream with fenced Observer projections.
waves.acceptance: Daily notes stream generates content-addressed SourceRecords with stable non-reingestion fence.

waves.objective: Act on Ryos and master-plan inventory: port launcher features to dotfiles and retire duplicates.
waves.acceptance: Duplicate decisions closed with dotfiles and PKos confirmed as sole operational anchors.

waves.objective: Generalize JARVIS action pattern to secondary commands with full approval and receipt lifecycle.
waves.acceptance: Preview, human approval gate, execution receipt, and recovery verified across multi-action surface.
